marble.name: Prepositions
marble.subject: English
marble.description: Understand and use the most frequently occurring prepositions of location and direction (e.g. to, from, in, out, on, off, for, by, with)
marble.prompt: If you ask you to describe where something is — like where the cup is on the table — can they use little words like "on", "under", "next to", or "by" correctly?

cluster.summary: Your child is learning the building blocks of writing — how to make complete sentences, use capital letters and punctuation marks correctly, and understand basic word types like nouns and verbs.

representations: Preposition phrase strips (in the cup, under the chair)
authoredAnswer: The pencil is in the cup. The book is under the chair. The ball is between the shoes. (Equivalent accurate phrasing, such as "inside the cup", is accepted.) The instruction uses a preposition that the adult can follow unambiguously, for example "Put the ball on the chair", and the ball ends where the learner intended.

wrongAnswers.revealedBy: Uses on for any contact position, or next to for any nearby position, regardless of the arrangement. Evidence basis: Common Core State Standards for English Language Arts, Language standards, Kindergarten. This is an aut
wrongAnswers.fix: Place the same object on, under and next to the chair in turn and have the learner say each; then let the learner set a position for the adult to describe.

wrongAnswers.revealedBy: Gives instructions using there or pointing instead of a preposition phrase, so the listener cannot follow without seeing the gesture. Evidence basis: Common Core State Standards for English Language Arts, Language standa
wrongAnswers.fix: Play a barrier game where the partner cannot see the pointing; model one preposition phrase and let the learner try again rather than correcting each word.
